newsitem.title: UK: LCH cuts margins on IPE natural gas futures.
newsitem.headline: LCH cuts margins on IPE natural gas futures.

text.p: The London Clearing House has reduced the margin rates it charges to buyers and sellers trading on the International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) natural gas futures contract, with the new rates taking effect from Tuesday morning, an LCH spokesman said.

The "scanning range" for natural gas at the National Balancing Point - the margin call which both buyers and sellers must put up as a security, and which is recoverable when the trade is successfully completed - is cut from 3 pence to 2 pence a therm.

And there are several other reductions, including a cut in the spread rate from 4.5 pence to 2.5 pence a therm; a cut in the spot month top-up rate from 3.5 pence to 1.5 pence a therm; and a reduction in the Seller's Security rate from 60 pence to 20 pence a therm.
Margin calls have already been cut recently, with a reduction from 3.5 pence to 3 pence a therm taking place in March.

A spokesman for the London Clearing House, which is the counterparty to every trade struck on the IPE, said that a reduction in volatility on the contract has allowed the cut in charges. He added that increasing liquidity on the contract and narrowing bid and offers spreads, as well as the fact that the market is entering the less volatile summer period, had all influenced the decision to cut rates.
The new rates apply with effect from the close of business on April 21, and are reflected in the margin calls from Tuesday April 22, the LCH said in a notice to IPE clearing members.
